links.outcome: Agreement of AI platforms versus human examiners on tear ferning grading against consensus
links.effect: Claude agreed best with consensus (4-grade weighted kappa 0.84; binary kappa 0.87), within interhuman range; ChatGPT and Gemini weighted kappa 0.48 each and underclassified abnormalities.
links.quote: Claude best matched the human benchmark, whereas ChatGPT and Gemini were less reproducible and systematically underclassified abnormalities.

unlisted_practices: Binary reclassification of ordinal grading scale to improve reproducibility

screen.reason: The study is a comparative offline evaluation benchmark assessing the reproducibility and diagnostic grading performance of multimodal foundation models (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) against human examiners on microscopy tear-film images.
